title: Does Expert Supervision Improve Text-to-Speech? An Empirical Study of Preference Optimization
authors: Minh Duc Vu*, Junchuan Zhao*, Ye Wang
summary: An empirical study of expert-guided TTS preference optimization across two student models, real and synthetic speech, and direct and bridge supervision. It shows why demonstration quality and target likelihood alone do not reliably predict improvements in generated speech.

title: X-MDD: LLM-Based Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis for Unseen Languages with Canonical References
summary: A multilingual pronunciation diagnosis model that combines canonical speech and phone references with in-context examples and GRPO. Trained on Mandarin and English, it evaluates transfer to Arabic without Arabic MDD training.

title: Edit Who Speaks, Control How They Speak: Global Timbre Editing and Local Instruction Control for TTS
authors: Junchuan Zhao, Chenglin Xu, Wei Zeng, Haoyang Li, Yiwen Guo, Ye Wang
summary: EDICT combines reference-based timbre editing with segment-specific expressive instructions, using an edited acoustic reference and KV-cache reconstruction to maintain voice consistency and acoustic continuity.

title: Preference Optimization for Non-Verbal Vocalization Synthesis
authors: Haoyang Li, Chenglin Xu, Junchuan Zhao, Yuang Cao, Liumeng Xue, Yiwen Guo, Eng Siong Chng
summary: A study of preference signals, pair construction, and DPO objectives for non-verbal vocalization synthesis, introducing a non-verbal-aware character error rate to balance vocalization realization and lexical accuracy.

title: AnyBand: Unified Multi-Bandwidth Speech Extension via Frequency-Aware In-Context Spectral Infilling
authors: Junchuan Zhao, Minh Duc Vu, Bowen Zhang, Ye Wang
summary: A unified frequency-aware framework for speech bandwidth extension across multiple input cutoffs, formulated as in-context spectral infilling.

title: Joycent: Multi-Accent TTS via Disentangled Accent Modeling and Layer-Specific Conditioning
summary: A diffusion-based TTS framework for controlling accent while preserving speaker identity. It learns speaker-disentangled accent representations and applies accent and speaker conditioning at different encoder layers, including cross-accent synthesis with separate reference prompts.
